title: Starting configuration for a statement
statement: Let $W$ be a word size and let $S$ be a compiler setting with frame size $F$, dispatcher position $D$, stack capacity $Q$, limits $	ext{lim}$, code, and code layout. For a statement $s$, state $σ$, code position $p$, stack-frame index $q$, and machine memory map $m:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{BitVec}(W)$, suppose the distinguished memory locations encode $1$, $0$, and $-1$ at addresses $-5$, $-7$, and $-9$, respectively; for every $n\le D$, address $-(25+4n)$ encodes $n$; address $-11$ encodes the stack pointer $-2q$; each frame-local address $-2(q+x)$ encodes $σ.loc(x)$ for $x<F$; and each address $a$ encodes $σ.mem(a)$ for $a<\text{lim.space}$, with all integers represented as $W$-bit words. Assume also that $1\le q$, $q+F\le Q$, the compiled code for $s$ in the setting's code layout is located at $p$ and its size fits before $D$, the width of $s$ is at most $F$, and $σ$ is bounded by the limits. Then the stack has room for the current frame and for $F+1$ additional cells at each of the remaining $\text{lim.depth}-d$ call levels: $q+F+(F+1)(\text{lim.depth}-d)\le Q$.
hypotheses_covered: Statement $s$, depth parameter $d$, state $σ$, code position $p$, stack index $q$, and memory map $m$
Memory encodings for the constants $1$, $0$, and $-1$
Memory encodings for every address below the space limit
The code size fits at or before the dispatcher
The state is bounded by the limits
caveat: The payload does not define the compiler setting, code-placement predicate, statement size and width, or bounded-state predicate, so those parts can only be described by their stated roles.
